doc.title: Jane Ira Bloom interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 3, 1998

title: Asteroid named Janeirabloom
summary: Bloom explains an asteroid between Mars and Jupiter was named after her, and that the astronomer listened to her space-themed CDs.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Being honored: NEA Jazz Masters and other awards

blocks.x: Soprano saxophonist and composer, and I recently learned that you are now in effect orbiting the galaxy. Can you tell me how that little thing happened?

Well last week I just got an e-mail from the Lowell Observatory in Arizona, announcing that an asteroid, which orbits around the sun, basically between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter, had been named after me. Asteroid 6083 Janeirabloom — with no spaces in between the names.
Tell me about your asteroid. I mean how big it is or —

I’ll tell you what the research assistant told me, who discovered it, he said it’s about three and a half miles across, it’s basically kind of a chunk of rock. It has a somewhat eccentric orbit around the sun, after its namesake, and it’s kind of new that they’re naming these things after artists. In the past they said they used to name orbiting planetary bodies and things like that after Roman and Greek gods. The research assistant said too many asteroids, not enough gods, so they turn now to naming them after other things.
Well it must be that obviously he’s listened to some of your music. Because you have managed to bring in the kind of space theme into some of your work.

Yeah. He’d listened to some of my CDs, which have a lot of titles that resonate from thematic spatial themes. And I guess when you’re sitting in the observatory late at night, you put the CD player on so he’s been listening to albums, you know, jazz albums.
